plain.li: Shirtsleeves weather, out of nowhere.
[winter] Warm enough for the icicles to drip, in the middle of winter.

warm.li: Let's eat outside while it lasts.
Open the doors and let the warm in.

blunt.li: Warm. Make the most of it.
Coats off, back to work.

cheerful.li: Summer's come to visit early!
I'm going to lie in the sun at lunch, don't stop me.

gloomy.li: The cold will come back twice as hard.
Enjoy it, it's only borrowed.

cold.li: Use the warm days for the outside work.
The woodpile lasts longer in weather like this.

plain.li: {ABOUT_nameDef} has seen our walls from the inside, and I'd rather that didn't go home with {ABOUT_objective}.
Mercy's a fine thing, {OTHER_nameDef}, but point it at someone who hasn't shot at us.

warm.li: I understand the kindness, {OTHER_nameDef}, but I'm afraid of what it'll cost the rest of us.
I don't want {ABOUT_nameDef} hurt, but I don't want {ABOUT_objective} free yet, either.

blunt.li: Let {ABOUT_nameDef} go and we'll be fighting {ABOUT_objective} again by spring.
No. {ABOUT_nameDef} stays where {ABOUT_pronoun} is.

cheerful.li: I like {OTHER_nameDef}'s big heart, but I'd like to keep mine beating too.
Can we at least wait until {ABOUT_nameDef} stops glaring at everyone?

gloomy.li: We'll free {ABOUT_nameDef}, and one night we'll pay for it.
It never ends well, letting them go.

cold.li: {ABOUT_nameDef} is worth more to us held, traded or recruited than simply released.
Releasing {ABOUT_nameDef} buys us nothing and risks a great deal.

plain.li: That's the year written down. Somebody else can write the next one.
We're still here, and that's the best I can say of any year out here.
The year's done. The fields will need turning in spring, as ever.

warm.li: Thank you, all of you, for another year.
We looked after each other this year. That's what I'll remember.

blunt.li: Year's over. Back to work.
That's another one. Next.

cheerful.li: Here's to the year gone, and the one coming, may it have more feasts in it.
We made it through another one! I say that calls for a cake.

gloomy.li: A year older, and a bit more tired.
I wonder who'll be writing this page next year.

cold.li: Year recorded. The colony stands, and the record shows how.
The year is closed. I'll use it to plan the next.

plain.li: Here's {TRADITION} again, and it comes round quicker every year.
It wouldn't be the year without {TRADITION}.

warm.li: I think {TRADITION} is my favorite day of the year.
It's good to do the old things together.

blunt.li: Right, it's {TRADITION}, so let's do it properly.
Tradition's tradition.

cheerful.li: It's {TRADITION}, my favorite!
I've been practicing for {TRADITION} all week.

gloomy.li: We keep {TRADITION} for the ones who can't.
Fewer of us for {TRADITION} than last year.

cold.li: Keeping {TRADITION} costs a day and buys a season of goodwill.
The colony is steadier for keeping {TRADITION}.

plain.li: It was mine for a while. I'd like it to be mine again.
I got used to having it, and now I notice it gone every day.

warm.li: I don't want to be ungrateful. I'd just love to have it back.
If there's any way to put it back, I'd be so glad.

blunt.li: It was mine. Give it back.
Asking again. You know what for.

cheerful.li: Second time asking, and I'm just as hopeful as the first!
Loved it while I had it. More of that, please.

gloomy.li: I'll ask, though I know how it went last time.
Asking for it back feels worse than asking the first time.

cold.li: I'd like it restored, and kept this time.
I'm asking again. How the council answers will tell me a lot.

plain.li: It was {NAME} again. I said the words, and the others said them back.
Kept {NAME} today. Fewer words than last year, and better ones.

warm.li: They all came for {NAME}, even the ones who don't believe a word of it.
Led the rite for {NAME} and held a few hands afterward.

blunt.li: Rite for {NAME}, done properly.
Short words for {NAME}, and true ones.

cheerful.li: Somebody started a song for {NAME}, and everyone joined in, which was better than anything I'd planned.
A good remembrance for {NAME}, with full bellies afterward and no one in a hurry to leave.

gloomy.li: I'll say the same words for {NAME} next year, and the year after.
Got through {NAME} with a cold in my chest and a heavier heart.

cold.li: Observed {NAME} correctly, every part in its proper order.
Conducted the rite for {NAME}. The colony is steadier for it.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} talked about the first winter {PAWN_nameDef} could remember, and how {PAWN_possessive} people got through it.
{PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} sat with the old maps and talked about the places on them.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} spoke to {OTHER_nameDef} of someone {PAWN_pronoun} once loved, long ago and far from here.
{PAWN_nameDef} gave {OTHER_nameDef} some advice {PAWN_pronoun} wished someone had given {PAWN_objective} at that age.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} exactly where {PAWN_pronoun} had gone wrong in life, so {OTHER_nameDef} wouldn't.
{PAWN_nameDef} warned {OTHER_nameDef} about raiders, and didn't soften any of it.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} confessed to {OTHER_nameDef} the most ridiculous thing {PAWN_pronoun} ever did when young, and they both laughed until they wheezed.
{PAWN_nameDef} taught {OTHER_nameDef} a song from {PAWN_possessive} childhood that no one else here knew.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} about a place that isn't there anymore.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} what {PAWN_pronoun} had learned about people, which was mostly to watch their hands.
{PAWN_nameDef} went through how the old settlements failed with {OTHER_nameDef}, so this one wouldn't.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, the chaplain, asked {OTHER_nameDef} for {OTHER_possessive} best memory of the one {OTHER_pronoun} lost, and then for another.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} held {OTHER_nameDef}'s hands and said nothing at all, and it helped.
{PAWN_nameDef} sat with {OTHER_nameDef} until {OTHER_pronoun} fell asleep.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} it was all right to be angry, and let {OTHER_objective} shout.
{PAWN_nameDef} put a bowl in front of {OTHER_nameDef} and said they'd talk once it was empty.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} got {OTHER_nameDef} to tell a funny story about the one {OTHER_pronoun} lost, and got a smile out of {OTHER_objective}.
{PAWN_nameDef} got {OTHER_nameDef} talking about the spring planting, and what {OTHER_pronoun} would grow.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} admitted to {OTHER_nameDef} that {PAWN_pronoun} still missed people {PAWN_pronoun} had lost years ago.
{PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} said the names of the dead together, one by one.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} found {OTHER_nameDef} something to do with {OTHER_possessive} hands and stayed while {OTHER_pronoun} did it.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} what each of them liked about the other, and waited until both had an answer.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} warned {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} that whoever started it next would be hauling for a week.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} got {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to agree on one thing, that last night's stew was terrible, and they laughed about it.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} about a feud {PAWN_pronoun} once watched end in a grave.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} wrote down what {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} each wanted, read both lists aloud, and pointed out they were nearly the same.

plain.li: One at a time, please.
We're not leaving until this is sorted.

warm.li: I know you both mean well, underneath.
Sit down, both of you, and I'll fetch us something to drink.

blunt.li: Quiet, the pair of you.
Shake hands, or shovel snow together.

cheerful.li: Let's all take a deep breath and a biscuit.
Come on, you two used to be friends.

gloomy.li: We can't afford to be at each other's throats.
There are too few of us for this.

cold.li: State your grievance, then listen to theirs.
This feud has cost us enough already.

plain.li: Counted out every sack for {PLACE} myself, and could tell you what's in each.

warm.li: Filled {PLACE}'s order to the last sack. I hope it gets them through.
We had enough to share with {PLACE}, and we shared it. That's a good season.

blunt.li: Delivered to {PLACE}. Every last sack.
{PLACE} got its order. Done.

cheerful.li: {PLACE} will eat well this season thanks to us, and I'm proud of every sack.
Full order for {PLACE}, on time, and not one sack split.

gloomy.li: What went to {PLACE} would have filled our own stores nicely.
Sent it all to {PLACE}. I counted twice and still worried.

cold.li: Filled the order for {PLACE} exactly, to the unit.
Delivered to {PLACE}. {FACTION} owes us a favor for the speed.

plain.li: Went to the gathering on someone's arm and left on my own feet. Slowly, but my own.

warm.li: The others kept checking whether I was comfortable. I was, the whole evening.
Sat with friends at the gathering and forgot I was ill for most of it.

blunt.li: Got out of bed for the gathering. Worth it.
Sore, but there. Good.

cheerful.li: I danced, sitting down, which counts.
Best evening since I got sick, and I ate two helpings.

gloomy.li: Tired before it was halfway done, but I stayed.
I watched them dance and remembered when I could.

cold.li: An evening among people did more for my recovery than another in bed would have.
I attended, briefly. It was worth the effort.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} asked me what I still believed, and waited while I worked it out.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} prayed with me tonight, and for once the words felt like mine.
{OTHER_nameDef} said doubt is part of faith. I'd never heard it put that way.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} asked about my faith. I answered truthfully, for once.
Good talk with {OTHER_nameDef}. Still doubting. Less.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I argued about faith all the way round the walls, and I enjoyed every minute.
{OTHER_nameDef} made the old teachings sound like good news again.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is patient with me. I don't know how long that lasts.
Talked about the faith with {OTHER_nameDef}. I wanted to believe more than I did.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} answered my objections one by one. I couldn't fault the reasoning.
A useful conversation with {OTHER_nameDef} about what we hold to.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} watched me work for a while and said one thing. It was the right thing.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me I was doing well. Coming from {OTHER_objective}, it meant a lot.
An afternoon with {OTHER_nameDef}. I hope I'm half as patient at that age.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} set me straight. Needed it.
Learned from {OTHER_nameDef} today. More tomorrow.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me about the old days, and some of it sounded made up, and I loved all of it.
{OTHER_nameDef} showed me a better way to do it, and now I can't stop doing it.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has seen so much. Most of it hard, by the sound of it.
I'm writing down what {OTHER_nameDef} told me, before I forget it, or {OTHER_nameDef} is gone.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} gave me three pieces of advice. Two were good.
{OTHER_nameDef}'s experience is worth more than {OTHER_possessive} labor now. I made use of it.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, the warden of guests, asked the {PLACE} what they were short of before they had to come and ask.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} went over to the camp and came back with three new songs from the {PLACE}.
{PAWN_nameDef} traded jokes with the {PLACE} until both sides ran out.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} heard out the {PLACE}'s worries about the winter and agreed they were real.
{PAWN_nameDef} sat with the {PLACE} while they talked about the hard road behind them.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} made sure the {PLACE} had dry wood and a fair share of water.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told the {PLACE} where they could cut wood and where they couldn't, and they thanked {PAWN_objective} for being plain.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} went over with the {PLACE} where the camp ended and the colony began, twice.

plain.li: I held a cup and talked all through {GATHERING}, which isn't the same as eating.
[diet:vegetarian] Meat in the stew, meat in the pie. I ate bread at {GATHERING} and kept quiet.
[diet:vegan] Even the bread at {GATHERING} had butter in it. I ate a raw carrot afterward.
[diet:carnivore] All greens and grain at {GATHERING}. My stomach growled through the toasts.
[diet:fungusinsect] Ordinary food at {GATHERING}. My people don't eat like that, so I didn't.
[diet:fine] Plain stew at {GATHERING}. I have standards, even here, and I kept them.

warm.li: Couldn't eat at {GATHERING}, but someone sat by me and shared their water.
I didn't eat at {GATHERING}, and that's all right. I was there, and they were glad I came.

blunt.li: Nothing to eat at {GATHERING}. Again. I'll say something next time.
Empty plate at {GATHERING}, and not one question about it.

cheerful.li: Nothing fit to eat at {GATHERING}, so I ate twice as much at breakfast.
I went to {GATHERING} for the company, and the company was excellent.

gloomy.li: They all toasted the cook at {GATHERING}. I'd eaten nothing to toast.
I sat at {GATHERING} like a guest at someone else's table.

cold.li: No provision for my diet at {GATHERING}. I'll raise it with whoever plans the next one.
Attended {GATHERING} without eating. Noted, for the next planning.

warm.li: Rest a minute, I'll take that.

blunt.li: Faster, there's daylight left.

cheerful.li: We'll be done by supper at this rate!

gloomy.li: There's always more of it than we thought.
We'll be doing this again next month.

cold.li: Two more loads and we're done.
Not there, over here.

warm.li: To the cooks, and the ones who carried the wood.

blunt.li: Drink up.

cheerful.li: Here's to a full table and no raiders!

gloomy.li: To another year of it, I suppose.

cold.li: To the colony, and its continued survival.
